claims.claim: EU Regulation 2023/956 establishes the CBAM, covering steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, and electricity.
claims.uncertainty: Covered goods list may expand in future reviews; current text is definitive for initial phase.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Compliance programs scoped to wrong product categories; exporters unprepared for inclusion.

claims.claim: The CBAM transitional phase requires EU importers to submit quarterly embedded-carbon reports from Q4 2023 through end of 2025.
claims.uncertainty: Transitional reporting methodology may be updated by the Commission before 2026.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Importers miss filing deadlines or use incorrect methodology, triggering penalties.

claims.claim: From 1 January 2026, EU importers must surrender CBAM certificates equal to the embedded carbon in covered imports, priced at the EU ETS carbon price.
claims.uncertainty: Implementing acts for the definitive phase may refine certificate surrender procedures.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Importers budget incorrectly for certificate cost; financial exposure mis-estimated.

claims.claim: Non-EU exporters without verified carbon pricing data in their home jurisdiction face higher effective CBAM certificate costs.
claims.uncertainty: Offset deduction mechanism depends on bilateral recognition agreements not yet all in place.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Exporters from countries with partial carbon pricing over- or under-estimate their net CBAM exposure.

claims.claim: Exact CBAM certificate prices for 2026 and beyond cannot be determined in advance.
claims.uncertainty: EU ETS price is inherently volatile; any forward estimate carries wide uncertainty.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Exporters and importers under- or over-hedge their carbon cost exposure.

evidence.name: EU Regulation 2023/956 establishing CBAM
limits: Legal text defines framework; enforcement depends on national competent authority implementation.
Certificate price is ETS-linked and cannot be read from the regulation itself.

evidence.name: EU Implementing Regulation 2023/1773 (CBAM transitional reporting)
limits: Covers transitional phase reporting only; definitive-phase mechanics are in Reg. 2023/956.
Methodology may be updated before 2026 definitive phase.

evidence.name: European Commission CBAM guidance
limits: Guidance may lag regulatory amendments and implementing acts.
Does not provide quantified cost-impact estimates for specific exporters.

evidence.name: European Parliament CBAM briefing
limits: Briefing predates final Regulation text; some details may differ from enacted version.
Secondary analysis; not the authoritative legal source.

unsupported_claims: Specific CBAM certificate price levels for 2026–2030.
Per-country compliance registration rates in the CBAM registry.
